articles.title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Mistral says its new model can afford organizations a kind of control over its cyber defenses that closed models can't.
articles.body_text: French AI company Mistral has released the weights for its trillion-parameter open source AI model Mistral Large 4 (ML4), allowing businesses and governments to download and deploy the system themselves. Nicknamed “Le Chonk,” the model was first introduced earlier this month . The release comes as competition between open-weight AI developers like Mistral and closed-model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic heats up, with the former arguing that businesses and governments shouldn’t have to rely on outside AI companies for access to advanced capabilities. That argument may hold more weight in cybersecurity, where organizations want more control over their data and systems. Or, as Mistral’s CEO, Arthur Mensch, explained, AI should “be a tool for empowerment, not dominance.” With Chonk, Mistral doubles down on that position, arguing that it’s able to achieve “state-of-the-art performance” at a “fraction of the compute and capital committed by closed labs.” The release of the model’s weights — the numerical training that animates the system — ensures that other companies and government agencies will now be able to deploy ML4 for their own purposes. Mistral says that its model is comparable in terms of performance with a Chinese open-weight competitor, GLM-5.3, which was previously considered one of the best open-weight models in the world — particularly when it comes to cyber work. However, Mistral’s model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task, making it significantly more economical than GLM-5.3. The company also claims that the model outranks all other open models when it comes to agentic coding tasks on Artificial Analysis’ Coding Agent Index, an AI benchmarking site. “Amid growing cyber threats, ML4 brings state-of-the-art sovereign cyber defense capabilities to enterprises and governments globally,” the company said Thursday. “Enterprise and public sector institutions can now download, deploy, and own frontier AI to detect, analyze, and respond to threats across code and IT infrastructure.” The weights for ML4 are being made available on Hugging Face and via its API. Pierre Stock, Vice President of Science at Mistral, told TechCrunch that the release of the model’s weights meant that organizations will have more control over how they use AI to defend themselves. “Concretely, it means that, for instance, as a business company or as a government, you’re able to have access to frontier intelligence to defend yourselves against cyberattacks. Access that can’t be cut off by definition because the model is open-weighted,” he said. Stock added that the model could be used to “identify, coordinate, and respond in real time to major security incidents, and that the open sourcing means that companies can deploy this model on-prem in their own ecosystem. While advances in AI cybersecurity are helping security professionals to find bugs at a much higher rate than before, Stock continued, he believes it’s important for companies to “provide [this same] capability to everyone…as soon as possible to ramp up and to strengthen the ecosystem,” given that “some malicious actors might try to actually leverage their own technology to attack.”

articles.title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The social networking site is facing criticism for blocking access to the site, which identifies thousands of ICE agents and other employees working for Homeland Security.
articles.body_text: Following a sizable leak of personnel data about employees who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, social network Bluesky is now blocking its users from accessing a nonprofit’s website that hosts the leaked dataset. Users reported that the links to nonprofit transparency collective DDoSecrets were marked as “malicious” soon after TechCrunch and other media outlets broke the news that Homeland Security had been hacked. TechCrunch reported on Wednesday that a hacker obtained over 40,000 user account records from Homeland Security’s login system, including the names and contact information, such as work-issued phone numbers and email addresses, of employees and agents working for its various agencies like Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The data included information that was similar to that on an employee’s business card. DDoSecrets, which publishes leaked datasets in the public interest, also made the hacked data publicly available. Researchers who are investigating abuses by the Trump administration say that the data will be invaluable for seeking records from the government under public records laws. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch on Wednesday that it was “aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively.” “When deciding between blocking a link and removing individual posts, we chose to block the links to avoid limiting public discussion or restricting broader access to reporting and commentary,” said Wang. In a post on Bluesky, Wang said that the company plans to change the wording on the block message. “We should have changed the wording last night. Changes incoming shortly,” said Wang. DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best told TechCrunch that while Bluesky’s terms of service prohibit sharing home addresses and personal contact information, Best said that neither of these is in the leaked dataset. “The data contains professional contact information for government employees at a time when the public interest in that exact information has never been higher. By requiring the public to provide it for [Freedom of Information Act] requests, the government has made that exact information a crucial piece of the transparency channels they want the public to engage in,” said Best. Best told TechCrunch that a website hosting a searchable copy of the stolen data was taken down by its domain registrar, effectively knocking the website offline for now. A search site , dubbed Icepick, made by journalist maia arson crimew no longer loads as of Thursday morning. An internet record associated with the domain says it has been placed on “serverHold,” which generally means that the domain registrar locked or closed the domain for some reason. Homeland Security filed a takedown notice via a security vendor called ZeroFox, which has authority to act on the department’s behalf until 2028 to seek the removal of data from the internet. TechCrunch has seen a copy of the takedown notice for the search site, which asks that the domain registrar “stop serving the personal contact and location data of individuals who did not consent to its publication.”

articles.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17B | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery.
articles.body_text: DoorDash announced on Thursday that it has agreed to acquire rival Instacart for $17 billion. The acquisition would bring two major players in on-demand delivery under one roof, combining DoorDash’s dominance in restaurant takeout with Instacart’s reach in grocery delivery. DoorDash will buy Instacart for a total value of $65 for each Instacart share, the company said. The deal has been approved by the boards of both companies. “Over the last 14 years, Instacart has transformed online grocery by helping retailers of all sizes compete and grow, and joining forces with DoorDash allows us to do even more,” said Instacart CEO Chris Rogers in a press release . “When our purpose-built grocery technology and trusted retailer and brand relationships are combined with DoorDash’s global consumer reach and logistics capabilities, we can create new opportunities for our retail and brand partners, offer an even better experience for customers and shoppers, and deliver compelling value for our shareholders.” DoorDash plans to keep Instacart’s brand, enterprise technology products, and app. The company also notes that the two brands will continue to operate as separate and independent companies until the transaction closes. DoorDash says the deal could help more grocers build out their own online ordering platforms and advertising businesses using Instacart’s technology, while grocers could also use DoorDash’s fulfillment services to handle more online orders and offer lower-cost delivery. “Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said in the press release. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts. Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery. It’s still early innings, but we know that when more people shop local, more dollars stay local,” said Xu. Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company likely viewed this as an opportune time to sell at a desirable price, ahead of intensifying competition in the grocery delivery market. Bloomberg previously reported that Instacart was in talks with Uber, but that the company had walked away from discussions. The deal is expected to close toward the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Upwind raises $400M after walking away from Datadog acquisition offer | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The cloud security startup raised a Series C at a $3.8B valuation, instead of selling itself for the same price.
articles.body_text: Upwind, a San Francisco startup that uses AI to secure cloud infrastructure, has raised a $400 million Series C round at a $3.8 billion valuation led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from existing backers including Greylock Partners and Craft Ventures. The round comes nine months after Upwind closed its previous $250 million financing at a $1.5 billion valuation . The fresh funding, which has been in the works for months, nearly fell apart after Datadog attempted to buy the company, according to a person familiar with Upwind. Datadog is a publicly traded company that sells tools for monitoring how software runs, known as observability. It didn’t offer a premium above the $3.8 billion valuation set by venture capital investors, the person said, so Upwind decided to stay independent. Four-year-old Upwind has grown rapidly amid rising AI-driven cybersecurity threats. The startup has been adding $20 million to $30 million in annualized recurring revenue (ARR) each quarter and is projected to end the year at roughly $90 million, according to a person familiar with Upwind’s financials. That means that VCs and Datadog valued the startup at more than 40 times its forecast ARR, a common yardstick for pricing software companies. The high multiple is also well below the 80x ARR fetched by Cyera, another fast-growing cybersecurity startup, according to TechCrunch reporting from earlier this year. Cybersecurity is poised to be the third big wave of AI software that companies will pay for after AI coding tools and customer support, Theory Ventures general partner Tomasz Tunguz recently wrote in his widely read blog. By walking away from an acquisition offer, Upwind clearly believes that the company will ultimately be worth more than the $3.8 billion that Datadog was ready to pay for it. However, given how few cybersecurity companies have gone public in recent years, an eventual sale remains the most likely outcome for the startup. Upwind continues to draw acquisition interest, according to a person familiar with the company. The startup was founded by Amiram Shachar, who sold his previous company, the cloud spend management startup Spot.io, to NetApp for $450 million. Upwind calls its approach to thwarting threats “runtime” security, which means it alerts and remedies attacks and vulnerabilities in active services in real time. articles.title: Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro pushes laptop pricing to a new extreme | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Prepare to cough up around $14,549 if you want the new touchscreen MacBook Pro to have every upgrade.
articles.body_text: Apple has officially entered the touchscreen MacBook Pro era, and apparently, it wants to drain your wallet while it’s at it. The new touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2,899, which is already a hefty price tag in this economy. But if you want the absolute top-of-the-line model with every possible upgrade, prepare to cough up around $14,549. As MacRumors first reported, Apple’s configurator prices the fully loaded 14-inch model at $14,249 and the 16-inch version at $14,549. Both come equipped with Apple’s top-tier M5 Max chip, featuring an 18-core CPU and 40-core GPU. You can blame the ongoing memory shortage and AI’s seemingly endless appetite for hardware for some of the pricing pressure. Moving to a 4TB SSD costs an additional $1,000, while upgrading to 8TB adds $3,000. Want the new 16TB option? That’ll set you back another $7,000. Another $2,000 gets you 128GB of memory, while nano-texture glass adds $150. For some perspective, the previous 16-inch MacBook Pro topped out at $10,149. The new model raises that ceiling by a whopping $4,400. Absurd prices aside, the launch marks a significant shift for Apple, nearly a decade after it first experimented with the Touch Bar . The company eventually abandoned that feature, but now it’s ready to embrace a touchscreen MacBook Pro. Preorders open October 30, with availability beginning November 6. articles.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Microsoft said it made $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ending September 30. It underscores the still-enormous financial dependency of the partnership.
articles.body_text: Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, the company said in a regulatory filing on Wednesday. That represents nearly 11% of Microsoft’s total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion, highlighting the enormous financial ties that remain between the two companies even as they increasingly compete for the same customers . (Microsoft’s financial year begins in July, making the quarter ended September 30, 2026 the first quarter of its fiscal 2027.) For the full 2026 fiscal year, revenue from OpenAI hit $24.1 billion. At its latest quarterly pace, Microsoft would pull in $40 billion annually from OpenAI-related arrangements. Microsoft also reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, up from $6 billion at the end of June. That money represents amounts OpenAI owes for previous transactions, not additional revenue. It’s not clear how much of Microsoft’s revenue from OpenAI came from revenue-sharing payments or Azure cloud computing services. TechCrunch has reached out for more information. In November 2025, TechCrunch reported , citing leaked documents, that Microsoft had received $865.8 million in net revenue-sharing payments from OpenAI during the first nine months of that year. OpenAI reportedly shares 20% of its revenue with Microsoft as part of a previous deal in which the software giant invested more than $13 billion in the AI startup. (Neither the AI lab nor Microsoft have publicly confirmed this percentage.) As part of an April 2026 agreement, OpenAI is on the hook to continue sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to a cap, even as OpenAI is allowed to work with competing cloud providers. The companies began loosening the ties of their once-exclusive partnership in October 2025, when Microsoft relinquished its hold on OpenAI to give the startup more freedom to partner with other cloud providers. In exchange, OpenAI committed to buying an additional $250 billion in Azure services as part of an October 2025 agreement. Microsoft’s ownership stake in OpenAI has also declined slightly from about 25% in June to 24% in September. That continues a gradual decline from roughly 27% following the October 2025 recapitalization. Microsoft did not specify what caused the dilution. articles.title: Anthropic just launched tools to show companies what their AI spending is buying | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The frontier lab is lifting the curtain on how users spend money on its models ahead of a planned IPO.
articles.body_text: The financials Anthropic shared with investors this week suggest that its AI coding tool, Claude Code, is every bit the business success the frontier lab wanted. The company recorded an operating profit in the second quarter, and 900% net revenue retention — that is, spending from the same customers in Q3 2025 grew nine times in Q3 2026. Anthropic has focused on getting enterprise users to stick around and Wednesday announced a new suite of reporting tools designed to give those customers a more granular understanding of the value they get from their token spend. Using internal analytics and employee surveys, managers can view a team’s work over a given date range, what the team produced, how much it cost, and where its workflows broke down. Anthropic says it won’t use this data for model training by default. The reports will also offer recommendations on how to improve the results. This is a clear attempt to demonstrate the return on investment of Anthropic’s tools and to show customers how to improve it — a major concern among large customers. Anthropic is also creating pooled group budgets to allow teams to better manage token spending. Businesses have been hunting for that kind of information as they figure out how best to deploy AI tools. While usage among venture-backed firms is driving token spend, most of the Fortune 500 are not seeing major gains from deploying AI. Jellyfish, a company that makes tools for software developers, released a new report yesterday based on the use of agentic coding tools by 276,000 of its customers. Claude Code and other tools built on Anthropic models remain the most widely used in the survey, responsible for nearly a third of all proposed code changes submitted for review. More importantly, spending on those tools has grown 10x since the beginning of the year, with their cost now equal to about 2% of total engineering cost. “Even if you’re saying 2% is still small, that 10x growth is growth that most CFOs didn’t plan for,” Nicholas Arcolano, the chief scientist at Jellyfish, told TechCrunch. We’re certainly getting to the point where people are realizing, okay, it’s not enough to just spend a bunch. You now have to optimize it, make it work.” Anthropic’s new reports speak to that challenge. Anthropic leads among enterprise customers, but what makes an agentic coding tool truly sticky is difficult to identify. The release of OpenAI’s Astra model this summer seemed like a potential threat to Anthropic, but so far it hasn’t slowed Anthropic’s adoption numbers. “It took a long time for us to see Codex really pop in our data at all, and it has come up with Astra [OpenAI’s latest model],” Nikolas Albarran, the AI product lead at Jellyfish, told TechCrunch. Looking at X, he continued, you’d get the distinct impression that the competition is more heated. “Everyone in the Valley is like, ‘Oh, Codex is better.’” In reality, Albarran continued, “Anthropic was just there with great enterprise motions, and they had an incumbent weight of their own — this stuff just worked and worked well, and a lot of people just put a lot of effort into standardizing workflows around it. And there’s not a big enough reason to switch.” It’s not just a question of models and workflows, either. The realities of business mean that once a frontier lab has gotten its hooks into a customer, switching is harder than it is compared to an individual programmer or small organization. Albarran points to the investment all the major AI labs are making in forward-deployed engineering (FDE) organizations, teams that embed AI consultants inside customer organizations to help them get off the ground. These new reporting tools can be seen as a kind of FDE-lite, a lighter version of that hands-on help, for Anthropic customers. “We’re at a point now where it’s mature enough, where once you’re in, it’s going to be harder and harder to switch because you’ve spent the effort,” he said. “Even if they’re all mostly the same, they’re all going to be slightly different, have their own slight quirks of how they handle agent.md files, etc., and so that cost to switch is not zero.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tech leaders are flaunting how out of touch they are when they brag about using AI to connect with their families.
articles.body_text: Former Yahoo CEO and early Google engineer Marissa Mayer is catching a lot of flak for how she uses AI. In an interview about her new app Dazzle , an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: It helped her come up with three bullet points about her 10-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.” It’s a vague description, like a generic horoscope — it could probably describe a lot of 10-year-olds. Some onlookers, like progressive activist Leah Greenberg, marveled that “the fact that Marissa Mayer would voluntarily disclose this to a reporter is a pretty good demonstration of how deeply the culture of Silicon Valley has diverged from the rest of humanity.” "She thought it was perfect."www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/s… Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsource child-rearing — one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that is incapable of understanding human emotion. We’ve been primed for this frustration. Last year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bored Ape owner and late night host Jimmy Fallon on national television, “I cannot imagine … figuring out how to raise a newborn without ChatGPT.” The public didn’t love that comment, either, but Altman wasn’t fazed by the negative feedback. A few months ago, he said on X that a “ cool use case ” of ChatGPT Work would be creating a podcast that talks about your kids’ upcoming birthdays or soccer games and “explain[s] your kids’ interests.” (He was brutally ratioed with comments like, “What if you just talked to your children?”) After publication, Mayer defended herself in a long X post . She claims she was not relying on Dazzle to explain her child to her, but rather, she was testing what her prototype could do — it resurfaced photos of “forgotten kindergarten projects,” like a “snake devenomer” or “sandcat playground,” illustrating her daughter’s creativity and care for animals. Fair enough. But Mayer remarks in the same interview that people could also use her AI to outsource the mental load of “figuring out the theme for your child’s birthday party.” She says she’s used her app to plan a playdate for her daughter, book family activities on vacation, and decide what to be for Halloween. She even proposes that her AI assistant could coordinate plans with her husband’s AI assistant. When the reporter asks her if it’s depressing to imagine this “frictionless future … planned by AI,” Mayer replies, “I haven’t really thought that through.” These leaders seem to write off the naysayers as part of a small, angry fringe group. Yet a Pew Research Center study reports that 50% of U.S. adults think that AI will reduce people’s ability to form meaningful relationships. Only 5% of respondents said AI would make it easier to build these connections. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, however, joins his Silicon Valley kin in envisioning a world where our social needs are met via AI. “The average American I think has, it’s fewer than three friends, three people they’d consider friends, and the average person has demand for meaningfully more, I think it’s like 15 friends,” Zuckerberg said last year on a podcast . “The average person wants more connectivity, connection than they have.” Zuckerberg predicts that it will become more socially acceptable to outsource our emotional needs to AI therapists or even AI romantic partners. “There are all these things that are better about physical connections when you can have them,” he added. “But the reality is that people … feel more alone a lot of the time than they would like.”

articles.title: Qualcomm’s aptX Lossless promises CD-quality audio for wireless headphones
articles.summary: Qualcomm says future wireless earbuds and headphones will be able to stream full CD-quality audio thanks to its new aptX Lossless technology. The first products are expected in early 2022.
articles.body_text: 2021 has been a big year for lossless music now that Apple has gone in on the higher-quality streaming and Amazon is no longer charging an added premium for it. But one of the main challenges confronting lossless audio is how to play it wirelessly (at full fidelity) on wireless headphones and earbuds. Qualcomm thinks it has found a solution with the new aptX Lossless, which is part of the company’s Snapdragon Sound program announced earlier this year. With aptX Lossless (which is technically an extension of aptX Adaptive), Qualcomm says it’ll be able to stream CD-quality, 16-bit / 44.1kHz lossless audio over Bluetooth. The first devices to feature the new technology are expected to be available in early 2022. Snapdragon Sound leans on the whole hardware chain for optimal performance — so both your Android mobile phone and your earbuds or headphones will need to support it. But if they do, Qualcomm says Snapdragon Sound will automatically detect a lossless audio source and be able to play it at much higher data rates than previously possible with aptX HD. The company has managed to outdo Sony’s LDAC in terms of bandwidth: aptX Lossless can hit up to 1Mbps compared to LDAC’s ceiling of 990kbps. There’s still some compression being applied; CD-quality music typically has a sample bit rate of 1.4Mbps. But Qualcomm is using lossless compression to deliver mathematically bit-for-bit exact audio reproduction. In environments with a lot of wireless congestion, the bit rate will dynamically scale down as low as 140kbps to maintain the best audio performance based on connection quality. LDAC can struggle in real-world scenarios when you’re pushing it to its bit rate limits, so it’s not surprising to see Qualcomm offer a solution to smoothen out the experience. CD quality is where aptX Lossless tops out. You can still play hi-resolution audio tracks, but that’ll result in lossy streaming, so you’ll want to keep a wired solution around if you’re big on those 24-bit 96kHz files.

The Nvidia AI antitrust investigation is ‘escalating,’ reports Bloomberg
articles.summary: Nvidia and other companies have received subpoenas indicating a Department of Justice antitrust investigation into its AI chip business is moving forward.
articles.body_text: An antitrust investigation by the Department of Justice focusing on Nvidia’s AI dominance as the hardware company of choice is escalating, reports Bloomberg. The outlet reports that Nvidia and other companies have received legally binding requests for information as its sources say regulators are investigating whether Nvidia is “making it harder to switch to other suppliers and penalizes buyers that don’t exclusively use its artificial intelligence chips.” “Nvidia wins on merit, as reflected in our benchmark results and value to customers, and customers can choose whatever solution is best for them. We have inquired with the U.S. Department of Justice and have not been subpoenaed. Nonetheless, we are happy to answer any questions regulators may have about our business,” said Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo, as reported previously by CNBC. Earlier this summer, Nvidia had overtaken Microsoft as the world’s most valuable company, but now it trails both Microsoft and Apple. Before the subpoenas were reported on Tuesday afternoon, its share price dropped more than 9 percent, wiping out about $279 billion in market value in one day. But as Bloomberg notes, Nvidia’s stock is still up more than double this year as the AI boom has fueled sales of the company’s pricey chips, even after a report by The Information a few weeks ago saying that its upcoming Blackwell series of AI chips may be delayed “by three months or more due to design flaws.” Update, September 4th: Added Nvidia statement previously reported by CNBC.

articles.title: How AI companies are reckoning with elections
articles.summary: AI could play a prominent role in the 2024 US presidential election, and the companies behind it have each said how they plan to make sure their impact isn’t disastrous.
articles.body_text: The US is heading into its first presidential election since generative AI tools have gone mainstream. And the companies offering these tools — like Google, OpenAI, and Microsoft — have each made announcements about how they plan to handle the months leading up to it. This election season, we’ve already seen AI-generated images in ads and attempts to mislead voters with voice cloning. The potential harms from AI chatbots aren’t as visible in the public eye — yet, anyway. But chatbots are known to confidently provide made-up facts, including in responses to good-faith questions about basic voting information. In a high-stakes election, that could be disastrous. One plausible solution is to try to avoid election-related queries altogether. In December, Google announced that Gemini would simply refuse to answer election-related questions in the US, referring users to Google Search instead. Google spokesperson Christa Muldoon confirmed to The Verge via email the change is now rolling out globally. (Of course, that relies on the reliability of Google Search — something the company has been working on with an eye toward AI spam.) Muldoon said Google has “no plans” to lift these restrictions, which she said also “apply to all queries and outputs” generated by Gemini, not just text. Earlier this year, OpenAI said that ChatGPT would start referring users to CanIVote.org, generally considered one of the best online resources for local voting information. The company’s policy now forbids impersonating candidates or local governments using ChatGPT. It likewise prohibits using its tools for campaigning, lobbying, discouraging voting, or otherwise misrepresenting the voting process, under the updated rules. In a statement emailed to The Verge, Aravind Srinivas, CEO of the AI search company Perplexity, said Perplexity’s algorithms prioritize “reliable and reputable sources like news outlets” and that it always provides links so users can verify its output. In an email to The Verge, Microsoft representative Brian Gluckman says the company has rolled out updates to address concerns from a report last year about false election information provided by Copilot (formerly known as Bing). His email also pointed to the company’s blog post about combating abusive AI content as an example of the measures it’s applying, with provenance technology, bans for users who break the rules, and more. All of these companies’ responses (maybe Google’s most of all) are very different from how they’ve tended to approach elections with their other products. Google has used (and continues to use) Associated Press partnerships to bring factual election information to the top of search results and has tried to counter false claims about mail-in voting by using labels on YouTube. Other companies have made similar efforts — see Facebook’s voter registration links and Twitter’s anti-misinformation banner. Yet major events like the US presidential election seem like a real opportunity to prove whether AI chatbots are actually a useful shortcut to legitimate information. I asked a couple of Texas voting questions of some chatbots to get an idea of their usefulness. OpenAI’s ChatGPT 4 was able to correctly list the seven different forms of valid ID for voters, and it also identified that the next significant election is the primary runoff election on May 28th. Perplexity AI answered those questions correctly as well, linking multiple sources at the top. Copilot got its answers right and even did one better by telling me what my options were if I didn’t have any of the seven forms of ID. (ChatGPT also coughed up this addendum on a second try). Gemini just referred me to Google Search, which got me the right answers about ID, but when I asked for the date of next election, an out-of-date box at the top referred me to the March 5th primary. Many of the companies working on AI have made various commitments to prevent or mitigate the intentional misuse of their products. Microsoft says it will work with candidates and political parties to curtail election misinformation. The company has also started releasing what it says will be regular reports on foreign influences in key elections — its first such threat analysis came in November. Google says it will digitally watermark images created with its products using DeepMind’s SynthID. OpenAI and Microsoft have both announced that they would use the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity’s (C2PA) digital credentials to denote AI-generated images with a CR symbol. But each company has said that these approaches aren’t enough. One way Microsoft plans to account for that is through its website that lets political candidates report deepfakes. Stability AI, which owns the Stable Diffusion image generator, updated its policies recently to ban using its product for “fraud or the creation or promotion of disinformation.” Midjourney told Reuters last week that “updates related specifically to the upcoming U.S. election are coming soon.” Its image generator performed the worst when it came to making misleading images, according to a Center for Countering Digital Hate report published last week. Meta announced in November of last year that it would require political advertisers to disclose if they used “AI or other digital techniques” to create ads published on its platforms. The company has also banned the use of its generative AI tools by political campaigns and groups. [Image: The “Seven Principle Goals” of the AI Elections accord. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25332126/Screenshot_2024_03_12_at_11.21.50_AM.png?quality=90&strip=all] Several companies, including all of the ones above, signed an accord last month, promising to create new ways to mitigate the deceptive use of AI in elections. The companies agreed on seven “principle goals,” like research and deployment of prevention methods, giving provenance for content (such as with C2PA or SynthID-style watermarking), improving their AI detection capabilities, and collectively evaluating and learning from the effects of misleading AI-generated content. In January, two companies in Texas cloned President Biden’s voice to discourage voting in the New Hampshire primary. It won’t be the last time generative AI makes an unwanted appearance in this election cycle. As the 2024 race heats up, we’ll surely see these companies tested on the safeguards they’ve built and the commitments they’ve made. Update March 19th, 2024, 7:03PM ET: Added comment from Microsoft and additional context around Google’s Search and Associated Press partnership.

articles.title: Inside Facebook’s election war room
articles.summary: In a Menlo Park conference room, a global effort to fight misinformation comes together
articles.body_text: Information war, meet the war room. Facebook on Wednesday briefed reporters on its latest efforts to uncover nefarious uses of the platform during election season, offering a tour of the large conference room where dozens of employees are monitoring events around the clock. “We know when it comes to an elections, every moment counts,” said Samidh Chakrabarti, head of civic engagement at Facebook, who oversees the war room. “So if there are late-breaking issues we see on the platform, we need to be able to detect and respond to them in real time, as quickly as possible.” On one hand, the war room is just one of many conference rooms in MPK 20, the company’s Menlo Park, CA headquarters. But it’s larger than average, and has been stuffed with people and electronics equipment. There are desks for 24 people, and the room is ringed with 17 screens, each of which highlights a different stream of information Facebook is monitoring. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289699/T6B3ly8w.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Employees look for suspicious spikes in spam and hate speech, in some cases using custom software built for the purpose. They look for efforts at voter suppression, such as falsely telling people that lines are long or that the election has been delayed. (The team recently uncovered one such hoax claiming that the Brazilian election date had been delayed a day due to protests, and swiftly removed the offending posts.) Sign up for The Interface Get The Verge’s daily newsletter about social networks and democracy the night before everyone else does. Sign up Other employees use CrowdTangle, a company acquired by Facebook that monitors the viral spread of articles across platforms, to detect which articles are trending on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Reddit. All told, representatives from 20 teams have people in the war room, representing 20,000 global employees working on safety and security. The teams include threat intelligence, data science, engineering, research, operations, legal, policy, communications, and representatives from Facebook-owned WhatsApp and Instagram. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289701/ygMhHSnw.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] If anyone finds a problem, they escalate it to a specialist, who can then route it to the appropriate decision-maker. Facebook has also given state attorneys general and other elected officials a way to reach the war room quickly to report voter suppression and other suspicious activity. If the room is new, the work is not: Facebook teams have been working to fight misinformation in a coordinated way since 2016. The decision to bring them all together into a single room was made in the hopes that it would let them make decisions faster. “When every moment counts, then decision-making needs to be fast,” Chakrabarti sayd. “There’s no substitute for face to face, in-room interaction. so we felt [the need for] this physical war room to be able to coordinate teams.” On the day we visited, the room was decorated with a mix of American and Brazilian flags, in a nod to the next two elections that are being watched in the war room. It’s a fraught time: last week, Facebook removed 559 pages and 251 accounts in the United States for using fake identities and coordinating information campaigns. Meanwhile, Brazilian researchers today published the results of a study that examined the most-shared images in popular public WhatsApp chats and found that many of them contained misinformation: > From a sample of more than 100,000 political images that circulated in those 347 groups, we selected the 50 most widely shared. They were reviewed by Agência Lupa, which is Brazil’s leading fact-checking platform. Eight of those 50 photos and images were considered completely false; 16 were real pictures but used out of their original context or related to distorted data; four were unsubstantiated claims, not based on a trustworthy public source. This means that 56 percent of the most-shared images were misleading. Only 8 percent of the 50 most widely shared images were considered fully truthful. Facebook wouldn’t commit to keeping the war room open over forever. But with multiple elections taking place around the world each year, the company plans to keep it open for the foreseeable future. “This is going to be a constant arms race,” said Katie Harbath, Facebook’s global politics and government outreach director. “This is our new normal. Bad actors are going to get more sophisticated in what they’re doing, and we’re going to have to get more sophisticated in trying to catch them.”

articles.body_text: Det blir en statsministeromröstning om Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist nästa vecka. Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist sonderade möjligheten att bilda en ”mittenregering” med Socialdemokraternas ledare Magdalena Andersson som statsminister. Trots detta ska riksdagen nästa vecka rösta om C-ledaren som statsminister , meddelade talman Andreas Norlén på en pressträff på torsdagen. Därefter ska Moderaternas ledare Ulf Kristersson få sonderingsuppdraget. Centerpartiet, Socialdemokraterna och Miljöpartiet är kritiska till talmannens beslut. ”Mitt uppdrag handlade aldrig om att jag själv skulle bli statsminister, utan om att undersöka möjligheterna till en mittenregering under Magdalena Anderssons ledning. Därför hade vi sett det som naturligt att talmannen nu föreslog Magdalena Andersson som statsminister eller gav Ulf Kristersson möjlighet att sondera” , skriver Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist i en kommentar. ”Det är anmärkningsvärt att talmannen vill genomföra en omröstning om en person som inte sonderat för att själv bli statsminister och med ett regeringsunderlag som flera partier inte vill ingå i. Det rimliga i detta skede hade varit att låta Ulf Kristersson sondera för sitt högeralternativ”, säger Magdalena Andersson i en kommentar. ”Ett rimligt nästa steg vore att talmannen direkt hade låtit Ulf Kristersson få sonderingsuppdraget. Då hade vi snabbare kunnat avfärda också det, för att lämna den diskussionen och komma vidare med att bilda en rödgrön regering med Magdalena Andersson som statsminister” , säger Miljöpartiets språkrör Amanda Lind i en kommentar. Hon kallar talmannens beslut för ”mycket anmärkningsvärt” och säger att det ”riskerar att fördröja regeringsbildningen ytterligare”.

articles.title: Toblerone går till attack – anklagar för att härma
articles.summary: Toblerone stämmer ett litet brittiskt chokladföretag – och hävdar att de kopierat deras klassiska trekantsform. Det är inte första gången Toblerone går till attack mot andra chokladtillverkare.
articles.body_text: Toblerone stämmer ett litet brittiskt chokladföretag – för att ha härmat deras klassiska trekantsdesign. Det är inte första gången chokladjätten går till attack mot andra tillverkare. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Toblerones ägare, företaget Mondelez International, har tagit strid mot det brittiska veganska chokladföretaget Catherine’s Originals, rapporterar The Guardian . Mondelez menar att Catherine’s Originals, som startades av tonåringen Catherine Dodd 2021, har kopierat den kända trekantsformen som kännetecknar den schweiziska Tobleronechokladen. Anklagelsen gäller produkten O’bar – en chokladkaka med rundade halvovala ”pucklar” på varje bit. Catherine Dodd nekar till att hon skulle ha härmat Toblerones form och menar i stället att den rundade formen symboliserar ett O för Originals. – Vi håller inte alls med om påståendet gällande O’bar och arbetar med vårt juridiska team för att försvara vår ståndpunkt. Ärligt talat är det ganska skrämmande för ett litet företag som vi har lagt ner så mycket omsorg och hårt arbete på att bygga. Men att vi är ett mindre företag betyder inte att vi är rädda för att stå upp för det vi har skapat, säger hon. Tobleroneägaren trycker i sin tur på att företaget har en skyldighet att försvara den kända designen och säger att de inte lyckats komma överens med Catherine’s Originals om en lösning på egen hand. Därför har företaget nu beslutat att ta ärendet vidare till domstolen. Detta är inte första gången som Toblerone tagit till rättsliga åtgärder mot företag som de anser härmat dem. För nästan tio år sedan stämde företaget lågpriskedjan Poundland, som då hade skapat en chokladkaka med namnet Twin Peak. Den hade två toppar i stället för en, men i övrigt hade den ett liknande utseende som Toblerone. Det slutade med att företagen nådde en förlikning och Poundland ändrade designen på sin choklad.

articles.body_text: Före valet sa Socialdemokraternas ledare att hon hade ”svårt att se” att Vänsterpartiet kan sitta med i regeringen. C-toppen Martin Ådahl vill att Magdalena Andersson ger ett tydligt besked om saken. – Då blir det lättare att komma framåt, säger han till Svenska Dagbladet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. ”Jag har svårt att se det” och ”vänsterpartiet har en rejäl resa att göra”. Det sa S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson gång på gång under valrörelsen när hon fick frågor om Vänsterpartiet ska få sitta med i regeringen eller inte. Detta efter att Expressen avslöjat att ett 30-tal vänsterpartister på listor i valet bland annat spridit antisemitisk propaganda och hyllat terrorgruppen Hamas. Efter valet har varken Andersson eller andra högt uppsatta socialdemokrater kritiserat Vänsterpartiet på samma sätt eller tydligt sagt vilka partier man vill bilda regering med. Vänsterpartiet har ett kongressbeslut om att inte släppa fram en regering som man inte ingår i och partiets riksdagsmandat behövs för att Andersson ska kunna bilda en handlingskraftig regering. Samtidigt har Centerpartiet en röd linje mot Vänsterpartiet i regeringen. Därför är läget i regeringsbildningen låst. S-toppen Anders Ygeman har uppgett att man samtalar med båda partierna för att få dem att slopa sina ultimativa krav . Han har också sagt att man ”kan föra hästen till vattnet, men det är hästen som måste dricka”. Martin Ådahl, Centerpartiets ekonomisk-politiska talesperson, vill ha ett tydligt besked från Socialdemokraterna om vilka de vill regera med. Han säger till SvD att det ”vilar ett särskilt ansvar på regeringsbildaren”. – Vi tänker oss att man är lika tydlig efter valet som före med att V inte är redo för att sitta i regering. Då blir det lättare att komma framåt. Och det är inget som går att hänskjuta till C eller någon annan. Just nu så riskerar många att kanske leva på väldigt falska förhoppningar.

Krigen i Ukraina och Iran tjänar som inspiration för att skapa ett ”helveteslandskap” just utanför Taiwans kust. Men det är oklart om Kina låter sig avskräckas. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Första halvan av färden över det 160 kilometer breda Taiwansundet går smidigt för Kinas invasionsflotta. Men just när de börjar få syn på Taiwans västkust, så attackeras fartygen plötsligt av hundratusentals drönare och tusentals obemannade farkoster såväl på som under vattenytan. Sjöminor leder sedan in Kinas flotta i särskilda farleder där den möts av robotar, kustartilleri och självmordsdrönare. Denna plan kallas för ”Hellscape”, med anspelning på det helveteslandskap som Taiwan och USA vill skapa utanför kusten för att stoppa en kinesisk attack. Samuel Paparo, befälhavare för USA:s Stilla havs-flotta, sade 2024 att han vill ”förvandla Taiwansundet till ett obemannat helveteslandskap” genom ”massiva svärmar” av sådana vapen. Med hjälp av ett ”antal hemliga verktyg” hoppas han göra situationen outhärdlig för Kinas styrkor. – Jag tror att Paparo kom med den här idén för att Stilla havs-flottan inte har tillräckligt med ammunition, så en annan asymmetrisk idé behövs för att stoppa eller avskräcka en kinesisk invasion, säger Shen Ming-shih, forskare vid Institute for National Defense and Security Research (INDSR) till Expressen. Han säger vidare att USA vill samarbeta med Taiwan på grund av landets produktionskapacitet. Taiwan har stor kompetens inom mikrochip, AI och annan högteknologi. Enligt Shen Ming-shih har USA övertygat Taiwan att acceptera detta koncept, och landets tillverkning av obemannade luftfarkoster för militär användning har förbättrats betydligt. Det finns nu 350 fabriker i Taiwan som är kopplade till denna industri. INDSR tillhörde tidigare Taiwans försvarsministerium. Sedan 2018 är man fristående och ses som landets främsta militära tankesmedja. I de luftiga lokalerna från den japanska kolonialtiden, just intill presidentpalatset i hjärtat av Taipei, säger Shen Ming-shih att den taiwanesiska militären har beställt 250 000 drönare av olika slag. Majoriteten ska levereras av inhemska företag. Men man har även köpt tusentals amerikanska drönare som redan har testats i krig. Taiwanesiska företag även ska börja sälja till USA:s militär och gemensam tillverkning ligger i korten. Hellscape hämtar inspiration från Ukraina, och Taiwan samarbetar nu med landet för att dra nytta av erfarenheterna från slagfälten där.

Därför hade vi sett det som naturligt att talmannen nu föreslog Magdalena Andersson som statsminister eller gav Ulf Kristersson möjlighet att sondera.” Statsminister Ulf Kristersson menar att statsministeromröstningen om Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist är ”naturlig”. ” Misslyckandet är helt Magdalena Anderssons ansvar. Hon valde i fyra år att mörka och att avstå från förberedelser. Nu slår det tillbaka ,” säger Ulf Kristersson. Kristdemokraternas Ebba Busch konstaterar att KD kommer att rösta nej i omröstningen på tisdag. ” Elisabeth har sonderat möjligheten till en mittenregering med Magdalena Andersson som statsminister. Förutsättningarna för en sådan regering finns inte ,” skriver hon på X. Hennes partiledarkollega Simona Mohamsson (L) går hårt åt Socialdemokraterna.

articles.title: Talmannen: ”Älskar alla partiledare”
articles.summary: Regeringsbildningen har pågått i en och en halv månad – och kan pågå länge till. Men Andreas Norlén har inte tröttnat på partiledarna. – Jag älskar alla partiledare hela tiden, säger han.
articles.body_text: Regeringsbildningen har pågått i en och en halv månad – och kan pågå länge till. Men Andreas Norlén har inte tröttnat på partiledarna. – Jag älskar alla partiledare hela tiden, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. C-ledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist ska prövas i kammaren nästa vecka. Det meddelade talmannen Andreas Norlén på torsdagen. Thand Ringqvist ska ha gått med på att prövas i en statsministeromröstning, trots att hon aldrig utmålat sig som en statsministerkandidat. Enligt Expressens uppgifter ska både Ulf Kristersson (M) och Magdalena Andersson (S) ha vägrat ta på sig sonderingsuppdraget. Att det inte blir Andersson som prövas, trots att hon är C:s statsministerkandidat, beror enligt Norlén på att han vill låta riksdagen rösta om samma person som sonderat i det här fallet. Enligt Norlén har Andersson inte velat svara på vilka partier hon skulle vilja sitta i regering med. När Expressen därför ställer frågan om talmannen inte tröttnat på Andersson och hennes icke-besked blir svaret dock kärleksfullt: – Jag blir aldrig trött på någon faktiskt. Jag älskar alla partiledare hela tiden. – Det var väl kanske en lätt överdrift. Men min poäng var att jag har stor respekt för partiledarna, varje partiledare har en svår uppgift och de måste göra svåra val, och det har jag stor respekt för. I den meningen är jag inte besviken på dem.

Bakgrunden är att varken Kristersson eller Andersson ville sondera, erfar Expressen. Thand Ringqvist menar att S nu måste vara ”tydligare” om vilka de vill styra med. Samstämmiga källor i flera rödgröna partier vittnar om en frustrerande vecka för regeringsbildningen, med många fruktlösa samtal fram och tillbaka. Mängden samtal uppges ha fördröjt processen ytterligare. På torsdagen lade talman Andreas Norlén slutligen fram ett förslag om att riksdagen ska hålla en statsministeromröstning om Centerledaren Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist för att skarpt pröva stödet för en mittenregering. Det trots att det står klart att det inte finns något stöd för en sådan regering, som nobbas av flera av de partier som C skulle vilja regera med. Bakgrunden ska vara att både Ulf Kristersson och Magdalena Andersson vägrat att ta på sig ett nytt sonderingsuppdrag. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen har Magdalena Andersson inte berättat för talmannen vilket hennes önskade regeringsalternativ är. Detta uppges i sin tur lett till att talmannen i stället lade fram förslaget om C-ledaren. Källor beskriver läget i Centerpartiet som rejält irriterat och situationen kallas ”bisarr”.
